title: Customer Networking Acceptance Criteria & Escalation Flow for Private Deployments
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Create a concrete, machine-actionable acceptance criteria checklist and an escalation flow that the Intake and Solutions teams can use to fast-assess Private/VPC/on-prem customer requests. Focus on networking constraints (e.g., egress/ingress requirements, proxy patterns), upgrade window capabilities, air-gapped environment constraints (patching, image delivery), and clear handoff triggers to Eng/Infra. Deliverables: checklist, decision matrix (green/yellow/red lanes), sample customer comms templates, and a runbook for escalations to engineering during pre-onboarding checks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A one-page acceptance checklist that gates customers into Fast-Track vs Escalation lanes based on quantifiable signals (network reachability tests, MTU and proxy config, patch cadence)
A2: An escalation flow diagram with SLAs for responses (24h initial triage, 72h engineering take-on for high-risk red-lane customers)
A3: Example probe commands and expected outputs (curl/traceroute/tcpdump snippets) included in the runbook for Solutions to run during intake
A4: Customer comms templates for each lane (Fast-Track, Remediation Required, Engineering Remediation) with recommended legal and security signoffs
triage_rubric: Network Reachability: green if >95% of control-plane endpoints reachable from customer VPC within region (measured via synthetic probe)
Proxy/Outbound Constraints: red if customer requires egress via strict outbound-only proxy with no mutual TLS or absent header passthroughs
Upgrade Window: yellow if customer can accept scheduled weekly patch windows but cannot accept forced live migration windows under 4 hours
Airgap Image Delivery: red if customer cannot accept any pull-based image delivery and has no documented offline image-signing/offload process
proposed_flow: Step 1 (Intake): Solutions runs automated network probe script and uploads results to ticket (script stored in Drive) - expected < 2 hours

Step 2 (Score): System assigns lane (Fast-Track/Remediate/EngEscalate) using rubric. Fast-Track => Solutions leads onboarding. Remediate => Solutions opens remediation checklist with customer. EngEscalate => route to Engineering triage channel with attached probes and proposed mitigation steps.

Step 3 (Escalation): For EngEscalate, on-call infra engineer paged (SLA: 24h ack, 72h working mitigation plan). Include risk score and rollback plan. Document decision in ticket and in customer readout doc.
Step 4 (Handoff): If remediation exceeds 2 sprints, create dedicated project and assign PM/SE to manage delivery timeline and contract changes
